x: Kharavela was defeated by the Asmaka king Satakarni, so the account is of Satakarni defeating Kharavela. Option A reverses this, saying Kharavela was the victor.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the animals were sheep and goats. So 1 and 2 only; '1 only' leaves out a true statement.
The civilisation is estimated to have covered about 1.3 million square kilometres and supported about five million people. Many settlements were located along the Ghaggar-Hakra system.

'Satyameva Jayate' comes from the Mundaka Upanishad (some sources wrongly say Mandukya). The Katha has the Nachiketa-Yama dialogue, the Chandogya has 'Tat tvam asi', and the Brihadaranyaka has 'Asato ma sadgamaya'.

Mahavira's birth is traditionally placed c. 599 BCE at Kundagrama near Vaishali (the date is debatable; some sources give 540 BCE). 527 BCE is the traditional date of his death and c. 468 BCE an alternative death date; 563 BCE is a date often given for the Buddha's birth, not Mahavira's.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: long discourses and the Mahaparinibbana Sutta are in the Digha Nikaya; the Anguttara is arranged by number and lists the 16 Mahajanapadas. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the false statement 3.

Pair 1 is correct: Borobudur is the largest stupa in the world. Pair 2 is correct: Sanchi is regarded as the largest stupa in India. Pair 3 is wrong: the largest stupa in Andhra Pradesh is Amaravati. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the wrong pair 3.

Veerapurushadatta was the Ikshvaku king who rebuilt the Nagarjunakonda Maha Chaitya and Sriparvata University; Vikramashila was a Pala (Dharmapala) Vajrayana centre, so A is the wrong pair. Naganika - Naneghat and Gautami Balashri - Nasik cave are correct, and the Sanchi toranas are a Satavahana gift (the south torana is credited to Siri Satakarni).

Statements 1 and 2 on Veerapurushadatta are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Mahavamsa says Mahadeva Bhikshu took Buddhism from Andhra to Sri Lanka, not the other way round. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the false statement 3.

Gosala spent about six years as Mahavira's companion before breaking away to lead the Ajivikas. Jain texts make Gosala Mahavira's disciple (some sources call him Mahavira's 'guru'), but never Mahavira a disciple of Gosala, and they did not stay in one order.

Statements 1 and 2 on the Ajivika lifestyle are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Ajivikas had no caste discrimination and appealed to warrior, industrial and mercantile classes. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the false statement 3.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the campaign lasted about 19 months; he died at Babylon in 323 BCE. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the false statement 3.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it was published in 1909; 1837 is the year James Prinsep deciphered the Ashokan edicts. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the false statement 3.

‘Andhra-bhrityas’ is a Puranic term, and one interpretation identifies the Andhras of Rock Edict XIII with Satavahanas serving as Mauryan feudatories. The evidence instead indicates that Buddhism existed in Andhra before Ashoka, making statement 3 false.
The Eastern Chalukyas (Ashtadasha Tirthas) and the Kakatiyas used the Saptanga and 18 Tirthas model. The Sungas, Kanvas, Indo-Greeks, Sakas, Kushanas and Western Kshatrapas are not linked with it.
The Arthashastra names the silver coin pana (karshapana). Kakani was a copper coin worth a quarter mashaka; Niska and Shatamana are not the Mauryan silver coin named in the Arthashastra.
Kautilya lists nine categories of slaves. Seven is the number of Megasthenes' social classes, and four and twelve are not Kautilya's figure.

Bharhut is called the most ancient stupa in India, while Bhattiprolu is called the most ancient stupa in Andhra.
⚠ Sources differ: the 'most ancient stupa' title goes to different sites in different texts (Bharhut, Sanchi, Piprahwa). This key follows the notes.
Gautamiputra Satakarni was the 23rd king, the last of the early Satavahanas (rulers 1-23). '28th', found in some sources, is an error; the 17th king was Hala and the 30th and last was Pulomavi III.

The G2 2017 key attributes the Yogasara to Kundakundacharya, who also wrote the Jain Samayasara. Some sources name Nagarjuna (author of Suhrullekha and Ratnavali) - the trap. Gunadhya wrote the Brihatkatha and Vatsyayana the Kamasutra.

In the context of the Deccan-Roman routes (Ujjain-Paithan-Tagara-Bharuch), the ship coins are credited to Vasishthiputra Pulumavi. Some sources also link ship-with-anchor coins to Yajna Sri Satakarni, but in this route context the answer is Vasishthiputra Pulumavi; Simuka and Gautamiputra are not credited with ship coins.

All four pairings are correct in the stated descriptions: Sanchi is the largest stupa in India, Kesariya the largest brick stupa, Bharhut the most ancient stupa in India and Amaravati the largest in Andhra Pradesh.
⚠ Sources differ: 'largest' and 'most ancient' stupa claims vary by source (Sanchi, Bharhut, Piprahwa and Kesariya each get superlatives). This key follows the notes.

Vasishthiputra Satakarni is credited with enlarging the Amaravati stupa, adding limestone sculptures and a stone railing (APPSC 2001 key). Satakarni I is known for the Naneghat yajnas, Hala for the Gathasaptasati, and Gautamiputra Satakarni for the Nasik prasasti, not for the Amaravati railing.

All three are correct. Statement 1: Sriparvatam is the Rajagirika centre per the APPSC 2012 key (some lists give Guntupalli). Statement 2: among the sects at Nagarjunakonda (Bahushrutiya, Aparashaila, Mahishasaka), Mahishasaka was the only Hinayana one. Statement 3: a Sinhalese vihara housed Sri Lankan monks. So D.
⚠ Sources differ: notes: Mahishasaka the only Hinayana sect in the list; but Bahusrutiya and the Theravada Mahaviharavasins were also non-Mahayana. This key follows the notes.
The G2 2019 key places Bhavaviveka's vihara at Sriparvatam; some sources say Dhanyakataka, but the exam key is Sriparvatam. Guntupalli and Salihundam are not linked to him.
Ajanta Cave 10, a Satavahana-era chaitya, carries the painting of the Shwetagaja (Chhadanta) Jataka (G2 2012). The Vessantara, Mahajanaka and Sibi Jatakas are not linked to this cave.
Kielhorn identified Sri Parvataswamy as the Buddha (G2 2019 key). Some sources credit N. Venkataramanayya, but that is the trap. Mackenzie discovered Amaravati and Sewell excavated it.
The Puranas list 7 Ikshvaku kings, while inscriptions confirm 4 (some sources say 8 and 5). '4 and 7' reverses the figures, and '8 and 3' and '30 and 7' match neither source.

The APPSC key (G2 2012) places Bodhisri's service in the reign of Ehuvala Chamtamula. Some sources put her under Virapurushadatta, but the key follows Ehuvala. Chamtamula and Rudrapurushadatta were Vedic kings.

Itsing (c. 700 CE) recorded Indian students memorising the Suhrllekha (G2 2012). Fahien and Hiuen Tsang are the trap options; Hiuen Tsang instead found the Sriparvata vihara neglected. Sung Yun is not associated with this account.

The wrong pair is C. The Khanapur plates come from Satara district in Maharashtra, and Ramatirtham is Indravarma's record, so neither belongs to the Guntur region. The other pairs are correct: Ipur and Velpuru are in Guntur, Chikkulla and Polamuru in the Godavari region, and Tummalagudem in Telangana.

The Pallava (Mahendravarman I) cave style of the 7th c. was later taken up by the Telugu Chodas and Eastern Chalukyas. The Kushanas, Guptas, Mauryas, Sungas, Satavahanas and Ikshvakus all came earlier, so could not take up a 7th-century style.

Statement 1 is correct: Meghavarman's request to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya is known from a Chinese source. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Fa-Hien travelled in Chandragupta II's empire but never names the king. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' leaves out true statement 2, while '1 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false claim about Fa-Hien.

C is correct: Toramana occupied Malwa and central India (up to Eran) but no Indian ruler is recorded as defeating him, while Mihirakula was defeated by Yashodharman of Malwa and Narasimhagupta Baladitya. Skandagupta fought the earlier Huna waves, and Rudrasimha III, Chandragupta II, Kumaragupta I and Samudragupta are not linked to defeating these two leaders.

Later Gupta gold coins were debased, with less gold and more alloy, and coins gradually disappeared as payments shifted to land. There is no record of more coins being struck, of Roman coins replacing them, or of Huna portraits on Gupta coins.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Sankheda copper plate is dated 594 CE (cited by some sources as the earliest dated place-value numeral); 876 CE is the Gwalior inscription. So A is incomplete and C and D include statement 3.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: lapis-lazuli blue is in fact used at Ajanta, though some sources claim otherwise. So A is incomplete and C and D include statement 3.
Govinda III defeated Nagabhata II. Dhruva's Pratihara opponent was Vatsaraja, not Nagabhata II or Nagabhata I (a common trap). Indra III defeated Mahipala I c. 916 CE, not Vatsaraja.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Dharmapala founded it, but it reached its zenith under Ramapala. Statement 4 is wrong: it is at Antichak in Bhagalpur district, not Banka (BPSC 2023 trap). So only A fits; B, C and D include a wrong statement.

The APPSC-GS 2018 key gives the Marturu inscription (an APPSC G2 2019 source names Kopparam; if both appear, choose Marturu). The Aihole inscription is Ravikirti's prasasti, the Satara inscription records Kubja Vishnuvardhana's appointment to Vengi, and Timmapuram is an inscription of Kubja Vishnuvardhana himself.

The key (G2 2012) credits Kollabhiganda to Chalukya Bhima I. Some sources give it to Vijayaditya IV, who ruled six months after Bhima: that is the trap. Ammaraja I bore Rajamahendra and Gunaga Vijayaditya III bore Tripura Martya Maheshwara.

The 2025 key makes Ayyana Mahadevi the queen of Kubja Vishnuvardhana. Some sources say Gunaga Vijayaditya III, but the key disagrees. Ammaraja II is linked to Chamekamba and the Kaluchumbarru grant; Vimaladitya married Kundavai.

The 2019 key credits the Kesari Samudra lake to Rudradeva. Some sources credit Beta Raja II with the Kesari tank, which is the trap; Vijayaditya VII and Rajaraja Narendra were Eastern Chalukya rulers with no link to it.
Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Potlacheruvu was a famous Jain centre, not Buddhist. Hence B; A, C and D all include the false statement 2.
The ASI recorded 17 inscriptions at Panchadarla in 1899, published in South Indian Inscriptions Vol. VI. The other series are not where these inscriptions were published.

The 2025 key marked 'Rajaraja Narendra built the Rajarajeswara temple at Biccavole' as incorrect, though some sources credit him with a Rajaraja temple there; follow the key. The other three statements are correct.

Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct: the 25 inscriptions (2nd to 16th century CE) copied in the June 2026 Nallamala survey include Pottapi Chola, Eastern Chalukya and Kakatiya records. Statement 4 is wrong: the records were not of the Pallavas only, and no Pallava records are named among them at all. So B; C and D include the false statement 4, A misses the Kakatiyas.

The Velanati line ended when the Kakatiya ruler Ganapatideva killed its last member (C). Some sources name him Mummadi Rajendra Choda and add that Nellore Choda Tikkana helped Ganapatideva kill Prithvisvara; Mallavarma was the progenitor and Gonka I the founder, so A and D are wrong.
A Kota chief married Ganapamba, daughter of Kakatiya Ganapatideva; some sources name him Bhimaraju II. This marriage reflects the Kotas becoming Kakatiya vassals.

Statement 1 is correct: the style is mature Vesara (Gadag style). Statement 2 is wrong: the material was chloritic schist (soapstone), not granite. Statement 3 is correct: stellate plans were a model later used by the Hoysalas. So '1 only' misses statement 3, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 2.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1025 CE Srivijaya expedition was led by Rajendra I, not Rajaraja I. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the plates use Sanskrit for the genealogy and Tamil for the grant. So '1 only' misses statement 2, and '2 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: they are Chola plates, and this was the first return of Chola copper plates. So '2 and 3 only', '1 and 3 only' and '1, 2 and 3' include the false statement 3.

Singhana II, who ruled from 1200 to 1247, was regarded as the greatest Yadava ruler and bore the title ‘Teluguraya Sthapanacharya’.
⚠ Sources differ: Singhana II's reign is given as 1200-1247 in some sources and c.1210-1246 in others. This key follows the notes.

Statement 1 is correct: Samanta 956-1162, sovereign 1163-1323. Statement 2 is wrong: the early Kakatiyas were Jains who later became Shaivas (APPSC G2 2011). Statement 3 is correct: their caste is given as Shudras and their official language as Sanskrit. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 2 are wrong.

Vidyanatha, court poet of Prataparudra II, wrote Prataparudra Yashobhushanam (APPSC G2 2011 key). Agastya wrote Nalakirtikaumudi, Balabharata and Krishnacharita. Ekamranatha wrote Prataparudra Charitramu. Sakalya Malla was a court poet, but he is not credited with this work.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: after Alauddin's death in 1316 Prataparudra stopped paying tribute. Hence A (leaves out 2), C and D (include 3) are wrong; B is right.

The APPSC G2 2019 key credits Kesari Samudram to Rudradeva (some sources give Prola I). Prola II built Arikesari Samudram (APPSC 2012), Ganapatideva built Laknavaram and Ghanapuram, and Mailamba built the Bayyaram tank.
Marco Polo is said to have described the extremely fine cloth of the region in this manner; the material is identified as fine muslin.

The Satavahana dancers' Maiputa is equated with Kusuma Lepanam (APPSC 2019). Perini is the warrior dance described in Nritta Ratnavali, madanikas are the bracket figures at Ramappa, and Desi is the regional dance form contrasted with Marga.
The Buddhist text Vinayavatthu mentions the 'Andhra Path' (APPSC 2019). Mahavamsa, Dipavamsa and Divyavadana are other Buddhist texts not linked to the Andhra Path.

Pedakomati Vema Reddi, the scholar-king (1402-1420), wrote Sangeeta Chintamani (PYQ 2011, 2019) as well as Sahitya Chintamani and Srngara Dipika. Kumaragiri wrote Vasantarajiyam on dance, and Kataya Vema wrote Kumaragiri Rajiyam. No work is credited to Anavema.

Vamana Bhatta Bana, at Pedakomati Vema Reddi's court, held the titles Sahitya Samrajya Dhurandhara and Sahitya Chudamani. Kavi Sarvabhauma was Srinatha's title, and Dharma Pratishthana Guru was not a title of Vamana Bhatta Bana.

Srinatha (Kavi Sarvabhauma) was Vidyadhikari, the minister of education, at Pedakomati Vema Reddi's court, and he composed Pedakomati's Sanskrit inscriptions. He held no post as chief minister, commander or royal preceptor.
Tikkana preached Harihara Advaita (the unity of Shiva and Vishnu; some sources say Harihara Dvaitam). He dedicated his Bharatam to Hariharanatha to reconcile Shaivas and Vaishnavas.

29 August, Telugu Language Day, is the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy; Telugu Language Awards are given the same day. Veturi Prabhakara Sastri identified the word Nagabu; Veeresalingam and Gurajada are not linked to this day.
The traditional four Agnikula clans are Paramara, Pratihara, Chauhan and Solanki (Chalukya). Some sources wrongly add the Chandelas, who are off the traditional list.

Modhera was fully solarised under an MNRE scheme (6 MW plant with 15 MWh storage), inaugurated on 9 October 2022. The court ruling on a temple concerned Bhojshala (MP High Court); Somnath Swabhiman Parv concerns Somnath; there was no 2022 UNESCO listing for Modhera.

All three statements are correct. Nicolo Conti was a Venetian who described the innumerable oil lamps at Diwali in Vijayanagara. Some sources place him at the end of Deva Raya I's reign, but the APPSC 2011 key placed this Italian traveller in Deva Raya II's reign.

Abdur Razzaq, the Timurid envoy to Deva Raya II's Vijayanagara, is credited with mentioning '300 ports'. ⚠ The APPSC key said Barbosa, so recognise that answer if it appears in an APPSC paper. Nikitin was a Russian horse merchant, and Tavernier described the diamonds of Golconda.
Muhammad Ghori granted Hansi (some sources say Kuhram) to Qutbuddin Aibak, the first iqta. Iltutmish later built the iqta into a system; Balban and Alauddin are not linked with the first grant.

Sultan Quli was killed in 1543; 31 years counts back to 1512, the start date some sources give for the dynasty, not 1518 (which gives 25 years). 1496 is when he became tarafdar of Telangana, and in 1517 he was defeated by Krishnadevaraya at Goni.

Statement 1 is correct: Urdu peaked under Abdullah Qutb Shah. Statement 2 is wrong: the 'Chaucer of Urdu' label found in some sources is for Ibrahim, not Muhammad Qutb Shah (whose pen name was Zillullah). Hence 1 only (A); B and C accept the wrong attribution, D rejects a correct statement.
The Tuluva dynasty was named after Tulunadu, identified with the Mysore region.

APPSC keys credit the Hazara Rama (Ramachandra) temple to Srikrishnadevaraya. Some sources say Devaraya II began it, but APPSC marks Krishnadevaraya. Achyutaraya built the Tiruvengalanatha temple (1534); Harihara I was the founder of the Sangama line, not the builder of this temple.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Sirimanu utsavam belongs to Paidithalli Ammavaru of Vizianagaram. So 1 and 2 only (A); B, C and D include the false statement 3.
The coalition is attributed to Rama Raya's diplomacy, interference, earlier attacks and sheltering of Jagadeva Rao; no Bahmani emperor created the coalition.
Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the grant was followed by Fort St George (1641, per some sources). So 1 only (A); B, C and D misjudge the statements.

One account describes the Gaz-i-Ilahi (about 82 cm) used under Zabti as bamboo, so C. Other sources say the bamboo item was the jarib, made of bamboo pieces joined with iron rings in place of hemp rope; either way, the material was bamboo, not copper, stone or iron.
Golconda agreed to an annual tribute, usually stated as two lakh hun, and to place Shah Jahan's name on coins and in the khutba. Some accounts express the tribute as two-and-a-half lakh rupees.
Aurangzeb's 1665 order fixed customs duty at 2.5% for Muslims and 5% for Hindus. The first option reverses the rates, and the others give incorrect figures.
Makhfi is best known as the pen name of Zeb-un-Nissa, Aurangzeb's daughter; some sources give it for Nur Jahan, so 'Nur Jahan alone' is the trap.

The standard answer is Humayun's widow Haji Begum (Bega Begum), who commissioned the tomb in Akbar's reign (c.1565-72). Some sources name Hamida Banu Begum, Akbar's mother, but not as the sole builder; Gulbadan Begum wrote the Humayun-nama and Jahanara built the Jama Masjid at Agra.

Annamacharya (1408-1503) was a contemporary of Saluva Narasimha (APPSC-G2 2011). Pedakomati Vema Reddy was Srinatha's patron, Abul Hasan Tana Shah imprisoned Bhakta Ramadasu, and Krishnadevaraya is not the ruler linked with Annamacharya.
The APPSC 2019 key names the Portuguese, who came soon after 1498. Some sources instead make the Dutch (factory 1605) first. The English came in 1611 and the French in 1669.

Narasapuram (with Machilipatnam) was a ship and boat building centre. Corangi was a Company-era shipbuilding site, not an ancient Satavahana shipyard, and Nizampatnam and Bheemunipatnam are not recorded as shipbuilding centres.

Pocock was the English admiral. D'Ache was the French admiral (some sources wrongly call the English admiral 'D'Eveche'), La Bourdonnais was the French Governor of Mauritius in the First war, and Conflans was the French commander beaten at Chandurti.

Jogipantulu used the Gollapudi mutiny to get the Circars leased to the Company for 15 lakh rupees a year (1766). 9 lakh is the reduced peshkash of the 1768 Treaty of Masulipatnam, and 7 lakh the Guntur payment of 1788.

All three are correct: Provincial Chiefs and Councils at Masulipatnam and Vizagapatnam governed the Circars; the supervising revenue body over these stations is called the 'Board of Revenue' in some sources; and district Collectors replaced the arrangement in 1794, when that body was abolished.

Statement 1 is correct: Mountbatten came after Attlee's 20 February 1947 statement. Statement 2 is correct: the Indian Independence Act of 18 July 1947 abolished the offices of Viceroy and Secretary of State. Statement 3 is wrong: the Interim Government under Nehru was formed in Wavell's tenure. Hence 1 and 2 only.

Nellore district was the world leader in manganese during 1892-1929 (APHQ 2019 key; some sources credit Vizag). Kurnool, Anantapur and Guntur are associated with cotton ginning, not world-leading manganese output.

The Hunter Commission is usually dated 1882; some sources say it was appointed in 1880. 1813 was the Charter Act grant of Rs 1 lakh, 1854 Wood's Despatch, and 1857 the founding of the three universities.

The Royal Titles Act 1876 gave Victoria the title, and it was proclaimed at the Delhi Durbar of 1 January 1877 under Lord Lytton. The 1858 Act only transferred power to the Crown; some sources wrongly place the title at the 1858 Allahabad Durbar. The 1861 Act and the 1911 Durbar have nothing to do with the title.

During his 1932–33 Andhra tour, Gandhi collected Harijana Bhiksha and launched temple entry at Siddhantam in Krishna district on 17 December 1933.
⚠ Sources differ: Census 2011 lists a Sidhantham in Penugonda mandal, West Godavari; the 1933 tour chronology puts the 17 Dec 1933 Siddhantam visit among Krishna district stops. This key follows the notes (Krishna district).
Osmania University, Hyderabad, conferred an honorary D.Litt on Ambedkar in 1953. Columbia gave him an LL.D in 1952; Andhra University and BHU are not linked to these degrees.

The 2011 key names Tatvabodhini (1864-70) as the first Telugu magazine from Bellary, although Satyaduta (1835) is also called the first Telugu journal. Hitavadi (1848) was from Masulipatnam. Vrittanti and Dinavartamani were Madras papers.

Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct (Vaijayanti/People's Magazine; Rajabahadur and Padyavinoda; Congress General Secretary). Statement 3 is wrong: he attended from Rajahmundry; Venkata Subbarayudu was the Machilipatnam delegate. So '1 and 2 only' misses 4, and options with 3 are wrong.

Statement 1 is correct: the Krishna District Association (1892) was the first in the Madras Presidency (APPSC-GS 2021). Statement 2 is correct: the APPSC 2012 key places its first meeting at Machilipatnam (some sources say Guntur - use the key). Statement 3 is wrong: Vizag followed in 1893. So '1 only' is incomplete and options with 3 are wrong.

Statement 1 is correct: he was jailed in 1922 (for one year; some sources say six months) for the song. Statement 2 is correct: he later served 2.5 years RI, during which his wife, father and grandfather died. Statement 3 is wrong: Gonedapadu, Narasannapeta taluk, is in Srikakulam, not Guntur. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses statement 2, and options with 3 carry the wrong district.

Prakasam's Swarajya (1921) was an English daily (APPSC 2011 key; some sources add Telugu and Tamil editions). Grama Swarajya was his separate weekly; Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao's Swarajya was a different magazine (a known trap); kisan publications from Nidubrolu were N.G. Ranga's.

It is the 1948 Act (APPSC G2 2008 PYQ: pick 1948). Trap: some sources call it the 1949 Act because it received assent on 2 April 1949 and came into force on 7 September 1949; estates were taken over from 1950; the Bill was introduced on 11 November 1947.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the 1881 Act followed the 1875 Bombay factory commission, and a 1895 commission could not precede an 1881 Act. Hence '1 and 2 only'; options with 3 are wrong.

The APPSC 2019 key names Madduri Annapurnaiah as first President; other sources give N.G. Ranga as President with Annapurnayya as secretary, so follow the key in the exam. Tenneti Viswanatham presided over the first conference at Guntur (1935). P. Sundarayya was a member and later Secretary of the Andhra Communist Party.

A. Subbarayalu Reddiar became the first Chief Minister in December 1920; the Raja of Panagal succeeded him in 1921. Rajaji headed the first Congress ministry in 1937; P. Subbarayan was not the first premier.

B is the intended key: Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao was president of the Vijayawada branch (the Andhra branches were at Hyderabad and Vijayawada, 1932). Maganti Bapineedu is listed as the Vijayawada branch's secretary, not Hyderabad's, so B's second pair is loose. A wrongly puts Nageswara Rao at Hyderabad; C names the national president and secretary (Birla, Thakkar Bapa); D names other women leaders.

Harijan was started in 1933 (January 1933 in some sources), with the first issue from Poona. 1919 is when Gandhi began editing Young India; 1903 at Durban is Indian Opinion; 1936 is the founding of Sevagram at Wardha.

Statement 1 is correct: on 4 February 1922 (some sources say 5 Feb) at Chauri Chaura, Gorakhpur district, the crowd burnt the police station and 22 policemen were killed. Statement 2 is wrong: the NCM was withdrawn in February 1922 after Chauri Chaura (Bardoli resolution); Jallianwala Bagh (1919) came before the movement began. So 1 only.

Sarojini Naidu led the Dharasana march, where volunteers took unarmed beatings, and Webb Miller of United Press reported it. Abbas Tyabji had been arrested before it; Kamaladevi led women into the Salt Satyagraha elsewhere; Louis Fischer was not the reporter.

Gandhi called the Cripps offer a 'post-dated cheque' and Nehru added 'on a crashing bank' (some sources give the whole phrase to Gandhi, with 'failing bank'). 'Dead as a doornail' was Nehru's verdict on Dominion Status in the August Offer; the other two phrases are not tied to Cripps.

The AICC met at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942 and gave the call 'Do or Die'. Wardha (14 July 1942) was the earlier CWC meeting; 6 August is a wrong date found in some sources; Ahmednagar Fort was where CWC members were detained after the 9 August arrests.

Gandhi launched temple entry at Siddantham in Krishna district on 17 December 1933.
⚠ Sources differ: Census 2011 lists a Sidhantham in Penugonda mandal, West Godavari; the 1933 tour chronology puts the 17 Dec 1933 Siddhantam visit among Krishna district stops. This key follows the notes (Krishna district).

C is correct as keyed: the APPSC G2 2011 key names Konda Venkatappayya the first APCC president, with his presidency given as 1918-23. Note that other sources name Nyapati Subba Rao first president of the 1918 Andhra Congress Committee, with Konda Venkatappayya as first secretary.
Wanchoo submitted his report in March 1953. Sources give differing exact dates within March, so the month is the reliable point.

Bipin Chandra Pal toured Andhra in April 1907 (Kakinada on 17 April, Rajahmundry 19-24 April) after Andhra leaders invited extremist leaders. Tilak, Lajpat Rai and Aurobindo did not make this tour. Some sources credit Mutnuri Krishna Rao with organising it; the APPSC G2 2011 key credits Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: it began in 1915 (some sources say 1916); 1913 was the first library conference. Hence 1 and 2 only; A omits 2, C and D include the false 3.

Nehru announced the SRC in the Lok Sabha on 22 December 1953, and it was formally constituted by Home Ministry resolution on 29 December 1953. 'August 1953' and '1954' are wrong dates found in some sources; 1 October 1953 was the formation of Andhra State.

Article 371D was inserted by the 32nd Amendment, 1973, implementing the Six-Point Formula. The 33rd is a common wrong answer (some sources print it); the 31st and 42nd Amendments dealt with other matters.

The State's tools against regionalism are the National Integration Council, Article 44, Article 51A and the Fifth, Sixth and Eighth Schedules. Article 32 (right to constitutional remedies) is not among them, so C is the answer.
The constitutional position is that secularism was part of the basic structure even before the word was inserted in 1976.

The Ravidassias renewed their demand for a separate religion code in the Census in July 2026. Jains, Parsis and Buddhists are already counted as separate religions in the Census, and all three are among the six notified minorities, so they have no such demand.

The Instrument of Instructions under the Government of India Act, 1935 is listed as an Indian antecedent of the DPSPs, along with the Karachi Resolution (1931), the Nehru Report (1928), Gandhian ideals and the Sapru Committee (1945). The Instrument of Accession joined princely states to the Dominion. The Objectives Resolution (1946) led to the Preamble. The Communal Award (1932) dealt with separate electorates.

The Collector’s judicial powers were separated in the Madras Presidency in 1816. This is regarded as an early instance of separation of powers in the Andhra districts.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: average attendance at the 16 DRSCs and the PAC was only 53% since the September reconstitution, and five meetings were postponed for lack of quorum. Statement 3 is the trap: there is no basis for saying the PAC held no meeting; it is one of the committees whose (low) attendance was measured. Hence '1 and 2 only'.
All four pairs are correct: Chandrababu Naidu was CM 2014-19, Jagan Mohan Reddy 2019-24, Chandrababu Naidu again from June 2024, and S. Abdul Nazeer has been Governor since February 2023.
The Election Commission set up 19 Appellate Tribunals under retired High Court judges for West Bengal roll disputes after the SIR. Bihar, Assam and Kerala are not linked to these tribunals.
More genuine federal bargaining is linked to the period after 1989, when coalition politics increased the negotiating power of regional parties.

The 13th Finance Commission recommended the National Disaster Response Reserve (APPSC-GS 2023 key); it also set the States' share at 32%. The 14th FC is known for raising the share to 42%. The 15th FC is known for adding demographic performance and tax effort. The 12th FC is not linked to the NDRR.

The 15th FC gave a first report for 2020-21 and a main report for 2021-26. '2020-25' is the trap figure that appears in some sources. 2015-20 was the 14th FC's period and 2026-31 is the 16th FC's. The 15th FC cut the share to 41% because of J&K's change of status.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the split is 4 Rayalaseema + 3 North Coastal, not 3 + 4. Hence '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' omits a true statement and the options with 3 include a false one.
The 1 July 2026 report highlighted low participation in Gram Sabha meetings. The other options (excess own-source revenue, completed J&K DDC polls, fewer AP Zilla Parishads) do not match the report.
Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Pradhans held unusual financial powers; therefore, statement 3 is false.
SVAMITVA is associated with the Survey of India and NICSI.

Anil Chandra Punetha is the AP State Election Commissioner who notified ward-wise photo rolls for 41 ULBs (12 corporations and 29 municipalities/nagar panchayats). The other names are not the current SEC.

The Lokur Committee (1965) gave these five traits for identifying Scheduled Tribes. The Kalelkar Commission is cited for the view that tribes may belong to any religion. The Bhuria Committee (1995) led to PESA. The Dhebar Commission is not the source of these criteria.

C is correct: the CIC declared INC, BJP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP and BSP public authorities in June 2013; they did not comply and the matter is pending before the Supreme Court. A is a trap from older sources: there is no such final 2018 ruling. B is wrong: the 2013 Amendment Bill lapsed. D is wrong: the 2005 Act did not name political parties.
Nine PSUs were given Navratna status and greater autonomy in 1997 (NCERT-based sources give 1996). 1991 is the year of the reforms, not of the Navratna scheme.

In August 2024 the Centre asked the UPSC to cancel its advertisement for 45 lateral posts after the debate on the absence of reservation in single-post recruitment. The Second ARC actually recommended lateral entry at Joint Secretary level, and neither a shortage of applicants nor a Supreme Court ruling was the reason.

An AP social-media task force was asked for by the AP Cabinet in July 2026, and it is among the July 2026 developments. The FCRA Amendment Rules are of 2026 (notified June 2026), not 2025. The Jan Lokpal agitation was in 2011, and the Press Council dates from 1966/1978.

Srinivas formulated the concept of dominant caste from his study of Rampura village in Mysore (1955). Mahuva is the site of I.P. Desai's study of joint family jointness; Kishangarhi and Senapur are not linked to the concept.
The Dhebar Commission (1960-61) flagged the least-developed tribal groups. The PTG category followed (dated to 1973), and it was renamed PVTGs in 2006. 1991 and 2011 are not linked to the renaming.

The listed measures are the SR Act 1956, the National Integration Council, Articles 44 and 51A, the Fifth and Sixth Schedules and the Eighth Schedule. The Eleventh Schedule (panchayats) is not listed. So '1, 2 and 4 only'; '1 and 2 only' misses item 4 and options with 3 are wrong.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct causes. Statement 3 is wrong: the identity crisis and generation gap grow as families become nuclear, not joint. So '1 and 2 only'; '1 only' misses 2 and options with 3 are wrong.

Statement 1 is correct: it is the standard definition. Statement 2 is wrong: the bases are caste, gender, disability, religion and region. Statement 3 is correct: these are listed practices. So '1 and 3 only'.
Optional creation, advisory powers and vacancies are weaknesses of SHRCs, and SHRCs in the highest-GDP States receive only 80 paise per capita.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: 'unequal treatment by society of men and women' is the definition of gender discrimination (APPSC 2024), not patriarchy. Hence A (1 and 2 only); B, C and D include the wrong statement 3.
Statements 1 and 2 on the WIA are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the NCWI (1925) was linked to the International Council of Women, not the ILO. Hence A; B, C and D include statement 3.

Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Women Help Desks are set up in police stations, and Mahila Police Volunteers are a joint MWCD-MHA measure. Statement 3 is wrong because MPVs only drew on the Nirbhaya Fund; they were not funded 'exclusively' from it.
The decline was credited to Shakti Teams, Women’s Safety Week rallies and Sexual Offender Sheets. There is no record that all police stations were replaced by women police stations.
The non-gender-neutral character of rape law is a criticism. The debate is not confined only to investigation speed.
The reservation is to commence only after delimitation based on the first Census after the Act, i.e. the 2027 Census.

Census 2011 records 1,241 caste groups notified as Scheduled Castes across States/UTs. 2,399 is the number of castes listed by the Kaka Kalelkar Commission (OBCs); 705 and 3,743 are distractors and not the SC count.

The K.G. Balakrishnan Commission examines SC status for Dalit converts to Christianity and Islam; its term was extended to 10 June 2026. OBC sub-categorisation is the Justice G. Rohini Commission's task; there is no ST creamy-layer commission or Rajya Sabha SC reservation.

B. The Kalelkar Commission itself used low caste status (with lack of education and poor representation in government service, trade and industry) as criteria; it was the Central Government that refused to accept caste as the criterion, so the report was not implemented. Options A, C and D are criteria the Commission did use, so caste is the intended answer.

The Commission, set up in October 2017 and given 14 extensions, submitted its report to the President on 31 July 2023 (some sources say October 2023); the report is not yet public. October 2017 is when it was set up; the other dates are distractors.

The Rampa rebellion (1922-24, Alluri Sitarama Raju) was a revolt against forest-law curbs on podu cultivation and forced labour in the Godavari Agency, so A, C and D are its issues. Zamindars were the target of the Santhal Hul, and land-grabbing was the issue of Birsa's Ulgulan, so B is the odd one out.

Per the APPSC 2022 key, the parliamentary standing committee on home affairs was taken to have recommended lowering the age, for applying POCSO, from 18 to 16. Note that the Committee's 167th Report (2012) actually backed 18; the APPSC key nonetheless treated the lowering claim as true. 16 to 14 is the December 2025 Private Member's Bill.

Yoga was inscribed on the Intangible Heritage list in 2016. 2019 is the year of Hyderabad's gastronomy designation and 2025 (December) is Deepavali's inscription; 2014 is not the year of any of these inscriptions.

The United States and Israel struck Iran's nuclear sites in June 2025, while Iran's Parliament weighed NPT exit in March 2026. Weighing an exit is not the same as withdrawing, and the IAEA has no power to authorise one.

On the AP side, Amaravati is a HRIDAY city. SPMRM develops Rurban clusters, SVAMITVA does drone surveys of village houses, and PM e-Bus Sewa provides city e-buses.

Budget 2024-25 BE allotted ₹47,277 crore to Welfare of SC, ST, OBC & Minorities, 31% above RE, making it the largest sector. It was not the smallest or cut, and it was neither fully centrally funded nor merged with health.
India is projected to become an upper-middle-income country by 2030; India is currently classed as lower-middle income (per capita income USD 2,760, July 2026), so it is not high income.

MMR = maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births (some sources wrongly say per 1,000). Per 1,000 mid-year population is the basis of CBR/CDR; per 1,000 live births is used for IMR; women 15-49 is the base of the maternal mortality rate, not ratio.

Uneven SHG quality, weak market links, debt stress due to poor financial literacy and political interference are identified challenges. An absence of political interference is not a criticism.

Quarterly buffer norms are fixed as on 1 April, 1 July, 1 October and 1 January (set by the CCEA); option A lists exactly these four dates in calendar order.

K.L. Rao proposed the Ganga-Cauvery link (some sources call it a Godavari-Cauvery link). Sir Arthur Cotton first conceived river-linking in the 19th century, Suresh Prabhu headed the 2002 Task Force, and the Prime Minister chairs the NWRC.
Glyricidia is a green leaf manure (PYQ key). Neem-based products are the bio-pesticides, Kamala is a genome-edited rice, and Nano Urea or Nano DAP are the nano fertilisers.

SMAM (2014-15 to 2025-26) set up 27,563 custom hiring centres nationally, and Andhra Pradesh had 239 CHCs in 2025-26 (75 of them with Kisan Drones). Some sources give a lower national count of 25,689; 25,260 is the number of farm machinery banks and 529 is AP's drone figure.
